result.title: How Far is Adam from Natural Gradient Descent?
result.summary: Adam is the standard optimizer in deep learning, yet its geometric relationship to natural gradient descent (NGD) contains unresolved questions. We study Adam's full update rule, including momentum, as a diagonal empirical Fisher approximation subject to diagonal truncation, empirical label substitution, and temporal lag. Using the scale-invariant $γ(Δθ)$ metric, we measure Adam's geometric deviation from true NGD across four loss landscapes: well-conditioned linear regression, ill-conditioned linear regression, logistic regression, and a non-convex small neural network. Adam's geometric trajectory is context-dependent. Deviation remains low in well-conditioned settings but rises significantly under ill-conditioning, reaching misalignments of $\approx 10^3$ in the neural network. Higher geometric drift correlates with slower initial optimization but does not degrade final objective minimization; Adam consistently reaches low loss. Furthermore, the improved empirical Fisher (iEF) tracks more stable paths than the standard empirical Fisher (EF), which frequently oscillates or diverges. Our results suggest Adam's practical optimization power may stem from a balance of structural approximation errors and momentum smoothing rather than close tracking of the natural gradient path.

AI.brief_summary: 该文把 Adam 的完整更新（含动量）解释为经对角截断、经验标签替换与时间滞后的对角经验 Fisher 近似，并用尺度不变的 γ(Δθ) 度量在四类损失地形上量化 Adam 轨迹偏离真实自然梯度的程度。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 无直接关系，但其中的「近似误差与动量平滑共同决定实际优化行为」以及偏离度量，可能可供核查 latent 状态更新与训练监督的贡献分配问题，例如 latent 轨迹是否也靠平滑而非精确证据追踪起作用。
